evidence.title: Mapping and predicting groundwater accumulations using remote sensing and aeromagnetic data: a case study from Bahariya Oasis, Western Desert, Egypt.
evidence.abstract: The Bahariya Oasis in Egypt’s Western Desert faces critical water security challenges due to intensive groundwater exploitation and limited renewable recharge. To address this challenge, this study integrates a GIS-AHP model for the first time in the Bahariya area and incorporates high-resolution aeromagnetic data to enhance the prediction of groundwater potential zones. Nine groundwater-controlling thematic layers were compiled from multi-source datasets, classified, and weighted using the AHP model: structural geology (lineament density), terrain (slope), hydrology (drainage density and rainfall), hydrogeology (lithology and soil moisture), land-surface conditions (NDVI and LU/LC), and the RTP aeromagnetic signal. The resulting groundwater potential map delineates coherent “very-high” potential corridors concentrated in the southern and southeastern sectors, where high lineament density, low-relief topography, and permeable Quaternary alluvial deposits coincide and correlate with known productive wells, suggesting favorable conditions for enhanced recharge and storage. Potential patterns also show strong spatial correlation with the drainage network and mapped structural trends. Model validation against well occurrences yields an AUC of 93.4%, indicating excellent predictive accuracy. Aeromagnetic interpretation further resolves the subsurface structural architecture and constrains the basement configuration, revealing a marked deepening of the basement toward the south and southeast. This is where a thick sedimentary cover suggests enhanced groundwater storage potential, providing additional support for the groundwater potential zoning results. This integrated workflow offers a robust tool for groundwater prediction and planning, with direct utility for prioritizing drilling locations and supporting sustainable water resources planning in arid environments.

evidence.title: Ensemble neural network models for stability prediction and optimization of hydraulic structures considering uplift pressure and exit gradient.
evidence.abstract: This study aims to develop a novel ensemble modeling approach that integrates artificial neural networks with finite element analysis to optimize the stability of hydraulic structures, particularly through the design of cutoff wall configurations. The research investigates the effects of varying cutoff wall positions and inclination angles on key parameters such as uplift pressure, seepage discharge, and exit gradient. Numerical simulations were performed using Geostudio SEEP/W to analyze seepage patterns across multiple configurations. The proposed methodology combines a Feed-Forward Neural Network (FFNN), XGBoost Regressor, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) with a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to create a predictive optimization framework. The findings reveal that the optimal cutoff wall inclination angle for minimizing both uplift pressure and exit gradient is 165° across all positions, while for seepage discharge, the optimal angle varies by position, ranging from 60° to 120° and increasing incrementally by 15° from upstream to downstream. The ensemble model demonstrated robust predictive performance across 5-fold cross-validation trials, achieving mean R-squared values of 0.99 ± 0.01 for uplift pressure, 0.94 ± 0.02 for seepage discharge, and 0.97 ± 0.01 for exit gradient. The small standard deviations indicate consistent performance across different data partitions, validating model stability and generalizability. The Genetic Algorithm results closely aligned with the numerical model outputs, validating the robustness of the proposed framework. This study introduces a significant improvement over traditional analytical methods by providing an integrated approach that enhances the safety and efficiency of hydraulic infrastructure design, particularly under complex conditions where conventional techniques may fall short.

evidence.title: Study on crack propagation law of overlying strata in the process of small coal pillar mining in inclined extra-thick coal seam.
evidence.abstract: Aiming at the problem of unclear crack propagation law of overburden rock in the process of small coal pillar mining in inclined extra-thick coal seam, this paper takes the 11,002 working face of Tengda Coal Mine in Heze, Xinjiang as the background. Through physical similarity simulation and 3DEC numerical simulation, the mining-related laws of small coal pillar working face in inclined extra-thick coal seam are clarified, and the height of caving zone and fracture zone are determined by combining multi-method weights. The results show that: (1) when mining in strike (dip), the fractal dimension of overburden fracture decreases rapidly in the range of 3-25 m (3-22 m) from the roof, the height of caving zone is 25 m, the height of fracture zone is 66.5 m (81.7 m), and the stress concentration coefficient is 1.17 in both cases; (2) The caving form of the whole overlying strata in the goaf is asymmetrically distributed, and a stable area is formed on the upper side of the small coal pillar, and the overlying strata do not collapse; (3) The subsidence and fracture rate of overlying strata show a vertical gradient decreasing law; (4) Using the weighted average method based on weight, the height of the caving zone is determined to be 24.98 m, and the height of the fracture zone is 81.67 m. The research results provide a theoretical basis for mining overburden control and gas control in small coal pillar working face of inclined coal seam.

evidence.title: Design, construction, and calibration of a weighable lysimeter for measuring water requirements of field crops for data-scarce areas of Ethiopia.
evidence.abstract: A simple weighable lysimeter was designed, constructed, and calibrated for measuring the water requirements and crop coefficients of shallow-rooted crops. It has a portable weighing mechanism to quantify changes in soil moisture content. The weighing mechanism consists of a horizontal steel bar, a hydraulic car jack, both ends hooked vertical steel bars, a stand, and a digital weighing balance. As the lysimeter's inner tank, a plastic drum with a 55 cm diameter that yields 0.24 m 2 of internal area was used. A performance test was conducted, and a rating curve was developed at the beginning of the growing seasons in 2023 and 2024 to evaluate the sensitivity of the weighing mechanism in determining crop water use. Linearity, repeatability, and measurement uncertainty tests were conducted. The linearity error was ±0.04 kg and ±0.03 kg for the years 2023 and 2024, respectively, which is within the allowable limit. The weighing system repeats the measurement perfectly with no error (repeatability error was zero). The combined uncertainty of the measurements was 0.023 kg, representing the cumulative effect of individual errors. The lysimeter weighing system is capable of detecting variations in mass as small as 0.2 mm of moisture content. Therefore, the developed lysimeter can be used to determine water requirements and crop coefficients of shallow-rooted crops for the design and management of irrigation in data-scarce areas of Ethiopia.

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.lesson: Any anti-fouling mechanism that relies on flow direction must be tested against RETROGRADE flow. Retrograde flow is a realistic clinical scenario (cough, Valsalva, venous pressure changes).

informational.mechanism: M3_REFINED electrothermal SMA retrieval
informational.lesson: ALWAYS report worst-case reliability for clinical devices. Averages mask catastrophic failure modes. Thermal activation in a 37°C body environment has a narrow window (37-45°C = 8°C max). Sensor electronics are a SPOF that cannot be fully resolved by redundancy (common-mode failures).

informational.mechanism: M5_REFINED adaptive over-drainage controller (sleep-state + venous pressure)
informational.lesson: Do not assume VP shunt problems apply to the eShunt. The eShunt's drainage geometry is fundamentally different (short path, no siphon). Always verify the problem exists for the SPECIFIC device geometry. Over-drainage is siphon-driven; without a hydrostatic column, it may not occur.

informational.mechanism: Flow reversal obstruction clearing (R3)
informational.lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

It provides a theoretical basis and technical support for optimizing reservoir fracturing design and improving the efficiency of CBM development, thereby addressing the issue of unstable production enhancement effects of the reservoirs. Physical simulation techniques mainly focus on pore-fracture structure characterization, rock mechanics testing, logging interpretation, and injection falloff testing in the well. Numerical simulation technologies mainly focus on geomechanics simulation, digital core simulation, fracture propagation simulation, and fracturing operation simulation. There are many problems in the current research. The results of indoor tests differ significantly from the field application effects. There is a lack of a comprehensive evaluation system that covers the coordination of multienergy systems, as well as environmental and economic factors. custody_records.raw_content: The Bahariya Oasis in Egypt’s Western Desert faces critical water security challenges due to intensive groundwater exploitation and limited renewable recharge. To address this challenge, this study integrates a GIS-AHP model for the first time in the Bahariya area and incorporates high-resolution aeromagnetic data to enhance the prediction of groundwater potential zones. Nine groundwater-controlling thematic layers were compiled from multi-source datasets, classified, and weighted using the AHP model: structural geology (lineament density), terrain (slope), hydrology (drainage density and rainfall), hydrogeology (lithology and soil moisture), land-surface conditions (NDVI and LU/LC), and the RTP aeromagnetic signal. The resulting groundwater potential map delineates coherent “very-high” potential corridors concentrated in the southern and southeastern sectors, where high lineament density, low-relief topography, and permeable Quaternary alluvial deposits coincide and correlate with known productive wells, suggesting favorable conditions for enhanced recharge and storage. Potential patterns also show strong spatial correlation with the drainage network and mapped structural trends. Model validation against well occurrences yields an AUC of 93.4%, indicating excellent predictive accuracy. Aeromagnetic interpretation further resolves the subsurface structural architecture and constrains the basement configuration, revealing a marked deepening of the basement toward the south and southeast. This is where a thick sedimentary cover suggests enhanced groundwater storage potential, providing additional support for the groundwater potential zoning results. This integrated workflow offers a robust tool for groundwater prediction and planning, with direct utility for prioritizing drilling locations and supporting sustainable water resources planning in arid environments.

custody_records.raw_content: This study aims to develop a novel ensemble modeling approach that integrates artificial neural networks with finite element analysis to optimize the stability of hydraulic structures, particularly through the design of cutoff wall configurations. The research investigates the effects of varying cutoff wall positions and inclination angles on key parameters such as uplift pressure, seepage discharge, and exit gradient. Numerical simulations were performed using Geostudio SEEP/W to analyze seepage patterns across multiple configurations. The proposed methodology combines a Feed-Forward Neural Network (FFNN), XGBoost Regressor, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) with a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to create a predictive optimization framework. The findings reveal that the optimal cutoff wall inclination angle for minimizing both uplift pressure and exit gradient is 165° across all positions, while for seepage discharge, the optimal angle varies by position, ranging from 60° to 120° and increasing incrementally by 15° from upstream to downstream. The ensemble model demonstrated robust predictive performance across 5-fold cross-validation trials, achieving mean R-squared values of 0.99 ± 0.01 for uplift pressure, 0.94 ± 0.02 for seepage discharge, and 0.97 ± 0.01 for exit gradient. The small standard deviations indicate consistent performance across different data partitions, validating model stability and generalizability. The Genetic Algorithm results closely aligned with the numerical model outputs, validating the robustness of the proposed framework. This study introduces a significant improvement over traditional analytical methods by providing an integrated approach that enhances the safety and efficiency of hydraulic infrastructure design, particularly under complex conditions where conventional techniques may fall short.

custody_records.raw_content: Aiming at the problem of unclear crack propagation law of overburden rock in the process of small coal pillar mining in inclined extra-thick coal seam, this paper takes the 11,002 working face of Tengda Coal Mine in Heze, Xinjiang as the background. Through physical similarity simulation and 3DEC numerical simulation, the mining-related laws of small coal pillar working face in inclined extra-thick coal seam are clarified, and the height of caving zone and fracture zone are determined by combining multi-method weights. The results show that: (1) when mining in strike (dip), the fractal dimension of overburden fracture decreases rapidly in the range of 3-25 m (3-22 m) from the roof, the height of caving zone is 25 m, the height of fracture zone is 66.5 m (81.7 m), and the stress concentration coefficient is 1.17 in both cases; (2) The caving form of the whole overlying strata in the goaf is asymmetrically distributed, and a stable area is formed on the upper side of the small coal pillar, and the overlying strata do not collapse; (3) The subsidence and fracture rate of overlying strata show a vertical gradient decreasing law; (4) Using the weighted average method based on weight, the height of the caving zone is determined to be 24.98 m, and the height of the fracture zone is 81.67 m. The research results provide a theoretical basis for mining overburden control and gas control in small coal pillar working face of inclined coal seam.

custody_records.raw_content: A simple weighable lysimeter was designed, constructed, and calibrated for measuring the water requirements and crop coefficients of shallow-rooted crops. It has a portable weighing mechanism to quantify changes in soil moisture content. The weighing mechanism consists of a horizontal steel bar, a hydraulic car jack, both ends hooked vertical steel bars, a stand, and a digital weighing balance. As the lysimeter's inner tank, a plastic drum with a 55 cm diameter that yields 0.24 m 2 of internal area was used. A performance test was conducted, and a rating curve was developed at the beginning of the growing seasons in 2023 and 2024 to evaluate the sensitivity of the weighing mechanism in determining crop water use. Linearity, repeatability, and measurement uncertainty tests were conducted. The linearity error was ±0.04 kg and ±0.03 kg for the years 2023 and 2024, respectively, which is within the allowable limit. The weighing system repeats the measurement perfectly with no error (repeatability error was zero). The combined uncertainty of the measurements was 0.023 kg, representing the cumulative effect of individual errors. The lysimeter weighing system is capable of detecting variations in mass as small as 0.2 mm of moisture content. Therefore, the developed lysimeter can be used to determine water requirements and crop coefficients of shallow-rooted crops for the design and management of irrigation in data-scarce areas of Ethiopia.
